title: Copper & pears — an oil study
goal: Retrospective baseline: explore oil mixing and texture in a still life.

inspiration.description: Copper pot and pears chosen for contrasting material and color

observations.text: Loaded pale dabs were swallowed by deep dark paint. The oil model was corrected to separate optical surface color from buried pigment.
Copper held its color after the correction; the repeated bristle texture remained stronger and more regular than desired.

nextExperiment: Use a small copper-and-pear calibration to reduce repeated bristle bands while keeping varied edges and restrained highlights.

title: Lemon at the blue hour
goal: Restrained highlights and varied edges: firmer lit shoulder, softer shadow side.

inspiration.description: An ordinary kitchen still life: a lemon catching evening light on a blue saucer. Original imagined composition, no external reference image.

observations.text: The soft table wash supported an angular open saucer outline. A broad center pass was needed.
Filled broad masses made the fruit and saucer readable. Yellow oil mixed toward olive.
Warm loaded oil remained subdued; the lower fruit edge stayed softer than the shoulder. Regular oil ridges remained conspicuous.
An acrylic light plane was also subtle; the green leaf balanced the blue saucer.
The final highlight remained very quiet. Lemon, leaf and saucer read together with ample bare linen, but the saucer stayed angular and repeated ridges remained unresolved.

nextExperiment: Paint adjacent small oil and acrylic highlight swatches on the same yellow ground before placing a fruit highlight; compare visibility and edge softness with the same renderer.

assessment.source: Live browser observations with final whole and close screenshot inspection. Provenance and journal written after export.

title: Golden fans, blue glass
goal: Curved, uneven leaf silhouettes and selective bright accents.

inspiration.description: Smithsonian Gardens description of fan-shaped ginkgo leaves; original imagined sprig in blue glass.

observations.text: Broad acrylic joined the S-shaped wash into a connected bottle mass.
Filled the hollow leaf crescents with tapering center passes.
A single loaded pale acrylic reflection was visible but quiet against blue.
Acrylic radiating veins read more clearly than the earlier pencil veins.

Shortened the pale notch stripe with yellow. Bottle mouth, dark base and trailing shadow establish glass and contact; leaves remain soft and the notch still reads partly as a pale accent. Regular simulated ridges remain visible.

nextExperiment: Repeat one ginkgo fan with radial broad strokes and a reserved unpainted notch; compare silhouette to the corrected pale stripe in this study.

assessment.source: Live whole and close browser inspections; journal added after export.

title: Small visitor, quiet morning
goal: Filled rounded forms first, selective crisp facial accents against softer breast and background edges.

inspiration.description: National Park Service chickadee page; original imagined bird and twig composition.

observations.text: Initial back and belly passes left an open gap; a broad center bridge filled it.
Pale cheek joined the floating cap to the body. Nape still needed a connecting pass.
Tiny acrylic eye glint was indistinguishable from simulated speckles; a larger dark surround and light touch were tried.
Two bent legs and a curved grip established contact with the twig.
Loaded oil produced a clear warm breast light, but regular bristle ridges made it read as a separate patch. Chalk feather edge remained subtle.
Broader acrylic transition did little to soften the oil patch. A smaller oil cheek light was clearer.
Thin oil transition remained ridged; final oil eye glint became visible. Filled breast, wing, beak and feet hold together; surrounding linen remains quiet. Stop to avoid competing accents.

inspectionEvidence: Actual whole and 2× close screenshots inspected in the browser at all 13 boundaries; screenshots retained in the task conversation. Replay records inspection camera boundaries.
nextExperiment: Compare oil, acrylic and chalk light swatches on the same gray ground, with matched brush sizes and short path lengths, before painting a bird highlight. Test thinner oil body for less regular ridges.

assessment.source: Live browser whole/close observations; provenance and practice entry written after export. Broadcast connected through at least 34 marks, then server stopped.

title: A small sea of green
goal: Varied curved edges and selective clear light accents against quiet water.

inspiration.description: Olympic National Park tidepool description sparked an original imagined green anemone, rocks and quiet water. No finished composition copied.

observations.text: Blue washes left a bare stripe; a bridge was needed.
Acrylic filled the disk, but green face lights remained subdued.
Thin oil made the four upper tentacles clearly visible; bends were angular and bristle bands regular.
Broad oil face joined the roots; two lower curves balanced the upright crown.
A pale oral ring and dark mouth established a focal center.
Narrower interleaved curves increased crown density and varied the silhouette.
A single small pale reflection stayed visible and quiet against the water.
Loaded acrylic closed the left slit after washes failed, leaving a darker water patch. Warm top and cool underside established the left rock.

Enlarging only the short lip accent made it visible. Unequal tentacles, a connected face and two restrained water reflections hold together. Regular oil bands and some angular turns remain; stop to avoid competing highlights.

inspectionEvidence: Actual whole and settled 2× browser screenshots at all 13 boundaries; camera moments retained in replay.

assessment.source: Live browser observations and final whole/close screenshots; journal added after actual canvas export.
assessment.improvementClaim: Corrections joined roots, filled the observed slit and clarified the focal light within this study. Thin oil still showed regular ridges. No controlled comparison or independent rating.

title: Two wings before the wind
goal: Filled curved silhouettes and restrained highlights; informal observation of thin oil ridge handling.

inspiration.description: NPS bigleaf maple description of double-winged seeds; original imagined still life.

observations.text: Filled acrylic sweeps established two unequal wings.

Fine acrylic ribs were nearly invisible over oil; broad acrylic did little to cover the oil light.
A single dark oil rib remained visible and followed the left wing.
Broader seed midtones filled the hollow crescent effect; a dark seam removed the pale central slit.
Curved oil stalk became legible; cool ground touch softened the straight contact base only slightly.
Enlarged short seed glint became visible. Unequal filled wings and quiet ground hold together; regular ridges and slightly hard base remain. Stop to avoid competing lights.

inspectionEvidence: Actual whole and settled 2× screenshots at 13 boundaries, retained in conversation; final screenshots saved. Camera moments retained in replay.

assessment.source: Live browser whole/close observations; journal and provenance added after export.

Loaded acrylic interrupted central pale band; oil moss became visible after acrylic moss was weak.
One short top-left cap light stayed visible and restrained in whole and close views.
Broader oil midtones closed the smaller cap wedge; unequal moss lights stayed quiet.
Contact shadows anchored both bases. Filled caps, unequal stems and quiet focal light hold together; regular oil ridges and angular turns remain. Stop to avoid competing lights.

observations.text: Three separate wash bands left pale gaps.
Broad oil pass filled the taper without a hollow center; regular ridges visible.
Extended quill connected to the spindle-like vane.
Three unequal brown bars visible; middle bar too solid.
5 px quill light almost lost in ridges.
13 px quill light visible; warm vane pass interrupted solid middle bar.
Projecting right barbs looked spiky.
Broadened roots became angular splits; chalk down remained faint.
Oil base wisps visible; contact shadow stayed quiet.
Outer bridges joined background washes, though pale bands remained.
Cool oil trim mixed into brown and enlarged tips rather than cutting them back.
Acrylic cooled the surrounding ground but did not fully cover oil tips.

Filled taper, broken bars, extended quill and loose base held together. Short shoulder accent stayed subordinate. Regular ridges, pale ground bands and angular splits remained. Stop because further cover attempts enlarged edges.

Outside watercolor bridges reduced long pale ground seams.
Short base contact anchored the kettle and copper collars attached handle feet.

title: Red pear, blue linen
goal: Build a filled red pear silhouette with overlapping broad passes and one restrained highlight visible at whole view.

inspiration.description: An ordinary red pear and folded kitchen linen sparked an imagined still life; no reference composition copied.

observations.text: Separated blue washes left pale seams.
Bridging reduced upper seam; first oil fold read as a stripe.
Broad oil overlaps filled pear body without a hollow contour; upright neck and abrupt right shoulder remained.
Curved right shadow turned under fruit; stem clarified identity; warm left pass ended abruptly.
Warm belly joined; widened cloth planes helped but squared ends and straight ridge dominated.
Left cloth end softened and short contact established; pear lacked a focal accent.
One 18 px cream oil stroke survived whole view as a small warm shoulder glint.
Dark socket attached stem and neck joined shoulder; lower background seam persisted.
Outside washes removed long pale seam; diagonal cloth pass broke ruler-like stripe.
Broad right cloth plane and warm lower turn visible; pale ridge subordinate to pear glint.
Short contact darkened, but reflected right edge became too bright and competed with shoulder glint.

Final glaze quieted reflected edge. Filled pear, warm-to-cool turn, attached stem and small shoulder glint held together. Regular simulated ridges and somewhat upright neck remained; stop to preserve quiet light hierarchy.

inspectionEvidence: Actual whole and settled 2× browser screenshots at 12 boundaries retained in conversation; final paired inspection saved under artifacts and camera moments preserved in replay.

title: Green wings after dusk
goal: Build filled pale wing masses before markings, vary edge hardness, and keep small eyespot and body lights subordinate to the green shapes.

inspiration.description: Original luna moth study sparked by the Missouri Department of Conservation field guide account of pale green wings, dark leading edges, four eyespots and long hindwing tails. No reference composition copied.

observations.text: Separated violet washes left two pale seams; granular edges visible.
Bridging washes removed bright seams; first forewing was a filled tapered mass with regular ridges.
Four filled wing masses connected, but upper pair read as narrow leaves.
Long tapered tails and pale body established moth identity; upper wings still too narrow.
Overlapping outer passes broadened and filled forewings; shapes became quite rounded and right wing had stronger bristle bands.
Plum-brown leading edges sharpened upper silhouette while lower edges stayed softer; pale head present.
Four compact dark eyespot bases stayed contained within wings.
Warm eyespot centers survived whole view with dark rims.
Small cool centers remained visible without overwhelming wing masses.
Head light survived at whole view; antennae looked blunt and leaf-like.
Quiet veins remained visible; denser curved tail paths softened angular bends only partly.

Fine comb marks broke blunt antenna shapes and short thorax light survived whole view. Filled masses, compact layered eyespots and unequal tails held together. Regular oil ridges and rounded forewings remained; stop to preserve quiet green masses.

inspectionEvidence: Actual whole and settled 2x browser screenshots at 12 boundaries saved under artifacts; final pair committed. Camera moments preserved in replay.

assessment.source: Live browser observations, paired final review and actual browser exports.
assessment.improvementClaim: Overlapping passes broadened narrow wings, layered spots remained compact, and fine comb marks broke blunt antenna shapes within this study. Tail correction was only partly successful; regular ridges remained. No controlled comparison or independent rating.

title: Where the forest drinks
goal: Build depth through separation of pale distant trees, dark framing trees and banks, then reserve the brightest short light for a small cascade.

inspiration.description: Original imagined forest stream, mossy fallen log and seedling sparked by Olympic National Park’s account of temperate rain forests and nurse logs; no reference composition copied.

observations.text: Atmospheric washes stepped from pale mist to a cool foreground but left horizontal seams.
Bridging reduced seams and a slightly warmer central opening remained.
Four distant trunks stayed soft and separated from the mist.
Dark banks framed a blue S-curve, but pale gaps and isolated bank masses remained.
Right foreground joined; dark trunks framed the scene and fallen log spanned stream.
Canopy and branches framed the opening, but paired wash clouds looked too regular.
Darker foliage and two middle trunks added layers; canopy remained broad.
Moss and underside separated log, but their strips looked divided by an unfilled middle.
Bark plane connected moss to underside; two unequal stones interrupted the banks.
Pool widened toward foreground and stone tops caught light; regular oil ridges remained.
Muted trunk lights and unequal roots connected framing trees to ground.
Dark ledge appeared, but first falling-water plane almost disappeared into stream.
Short brighter fall survived whole view; long dark foreground ripple was too strong.
Nearer stones varied foreground scale and stayed quieter than the cascade.
Hanging moss broke log underside; canopy leaf accents still looked like smooth bars.
Unequal foreground fern fronds read clearly but as solid blades.
Alternating leaflet cuts broke fern blades at whole view but remained stylized.
Cover pass interrupted dark ripple with visible mixing; short shadows anchored stones.
Seedling rooted visibly in log moss, with two unequal small leaves.
Shadow cuts interrupted canopy bars and short bark breaks varied smooth trunks.
Small right-bank plant stayed below fern scale; left stone gained darker lower facet.
Facets broke dark cascade ledge and brief foam marks distinguished falling from flat water.
Moss notches, bark fissure and knot interrupted log’s long surface.
New stone accents became isolated bright dots that competed with cascade; seedling veins remained small.

Broader muted passes softened stone dots but enlarged their light areas. Short cascade strengthened as brightest accent, and pool ripple shortened with visible cover mixing. Pale distance, dark banks, connected log and seedling held together. Rounded foliage, stylized fern cuts, acrylic speckles and regular oil ridges remained. Stop to avoid building competing lights.

inspectionEvidence: Actual paired whole and settled 2x close browser screenshots at 25 distinct boundaries retained under artifacts. Framing corrections prompted repeat pairs at 4 and 64. Final pair committed; all live notes and camera moments preserved in replay.
nextExperiment: Repeat a small three-plane forest composition with a fixed palette and renderer. Compare one short acrylic water light to oil at matched size, flow and pressure; keep stone lights at least one value darker. Measure by paired visual review rather than stroke count.

assessment.source: Live browser observations, final paired review and actual browser exports.
assessment.improvementClaim: The longer session allowed joined ground bands, log-plane correction, bank contacts, seedling, fern and a revised light hierarchy. Several corrections were partial: pool covering mixed visibly, stone lights widened, canopy remained rounded and oil ridges stayed regular. More marks do not establish improvement; no controlled comparison or independent rating.

title: October, folded blue
goal: Turn uneven pumpkin ribs with warm and cool planes, reserving the strongest light for one short shoulder accent.

inspiration.description: Squash in the NPS Three Sisters garden sparked an imagined pumpkin and fallen leaf on folded blue cloth; composition is original.

observations.text: Broad overlapping oil passes closed three holes left by the pumpkin outline.
Broad neighboring orange planes quieted the initially stripe-like dark troughs, only partly.
Thin oil altered the long shadow end more visibly than the earlier acrylic cover; regular ridges persisted.
A filled upper plane and a folded lip made the small curled leaf readable; lip remained heavy. Lower/right panned close inspection confirmed it.
Vertical and diagonal washes reduced the stacked ground bands; pale seams remained at the margins.
A single short shoulder light survived whole view and established the focal accent.
Grey contour covers formed bars within the shoulders; warm covers reduced them only partly.

Final refinement kept a warm left shoulder, darker right plane, bent cut stem, connected blue folds and a subordinate leaf. Reflected-edge correction remained partial. Faceted shoulders, regular oil ridges and cover mixing remained; stopped to avoid further thickening the edges.

inspectionEvidence: Initial 4/8 captures had framing errors; corrected full-page paired visual inspections from 12 onward. Additional lower/right panned leaf inspection at 64. A screenshot filename reuse error overwrote intermediate pairs; final 112 whole/close pair and leaf pan retained. The 29 inspection boundaries were observed live; intermediate files are not all retained.
nextExperiment: Repeat a three-rib squash at fixed palette and renderer with 48 marks. Compare softly filled rib planes with narrow troughs; test a short oil cover beside acrylic over an oil shadow at matched size and flow. Keep the first shoulder light and avoid grey contour-cover stripes.

assessment.source: Live browser observations, paired screenshots, actual browser PNG/session exports and public ended-feed receipt.
assessment.improvementClaim: No controlled comparison or human rating. Filled masses and quieter focal light worked; edge-cover corrections were partial and regular simulated texture remained.

title: Still water, long shadow
goal: Keep a bent heron neck readable with a few broad planes and reserve the brightest accent for the head.

inspiration.description: NPS Great Marsh description sparked an original imagined heron among cattails; no finished composition copied.

observations.text: Broad overlapping passes closed the hollow hooked belly.
Loaded pale oil neck plane separated the bent neck from cool water.
Watercolor barely altered the oil bank; a thin oil cover widened it rather than dissolving its edge.
Panned head close-up confirmed small amber eye beneath heavy crown.
Short brow light stayed small at whole view; throat cover was partial and ridged.
Six-point narrow leaf gestures made gentler arcs than earlier three-point elbows.
Longer feather planes separated wing, but the new shoulder light competed with the head.
Muted shoulder restored head emphasis; tapering over blunt tail was partial.
Low ripples interrupted flat foot bars. Water-color oil cover created grey tail extension.

Final brow, cheek and tapered breast refinement kept head light small, bent neck readable, filled body, unequal grasses and quiet reflection. Angular shoulders, regular oil ridges, ribbon banks and grey tail-cover extension remain. Stopped because additional covers enlarged edges.

inspectionEvidence: 26 paired inspection boundaries. First 4 whole/close observed live but not retained. Whole capture at 12 initially caught camera transition; repeated and replaced after correction. Settled whole/2x close screenshots retained from 8 onward with unique numeric names; additional head pan at 61. Final paired 100 images committed.
nextExperiment: Repeat a small bent-neck bird with fixed palette and renderer, comparing three-point and six-point curved strokes at matched size and pressure. Test edge cover on an isolated swatch before using it on the silhouette.

assessment.source: Live browser observations, final paired review and actual browser exports.

Broad loaded oil overlaps closed the forked hollow tube and established a dark mouth.
Broader leaf middles filled seams; blunt round ends remained despite taper extensions at 44.
Loaded ivory fold survived whole view and separated outer wall from cool throat.
Low-load watercolor gestures barely changed the dry bands. Thin oil stems at 80 made a clearer interruption.
Cool fold became an isolated blue slash at 84; broad ivory overlap reduced it.
Single short loaded ivory lip stroke stayed compact and visible at whole view.

Final refinement quieted a long leaf vein and softened mouth and petal transitions. Joined trumpet, unequal leaves, hanging bud and small focal light hold. Faceted rim, angular bud, rounded leaf ends and regular oil ridges remain.

title: Wind timber

inspiration.description: NPS Bryce Canyon bristlecone guide sparked an original imagined twisted pine above a cool stony basin; no finished composition copied.

observations.text: Broad warm passes filled and turned the joined dark trunk; roots initially made a flat fork.
Overlapping stones hid the blunt lower trunk and helped anchor the roots.
Loaded wood ribbon was clearer than earlier thin stone lights; narrow grain channel turned the trunk.
Broader overlaps joined initially detached left needle crescents; cap-like canopy edges remained. Upper pan confirmed branch elbows and joins.
Crossed watercolor interrupted the pale horizon stripe into shorter fragments rather than erasing it.
Loaded acrylic barely changed the earlier oil stones at whole view; this was not a controlled media comparison.
A single short loaded light stayed compact and visible at whole view.
Partial soil covers added ridged patches and reduced little of the straight contact bars.
Long fine needle ends became visible beneath the caps.
Warm overlap joined the dark branch stub into the trunk collar.

Final grain-end and root-collar refinement preserved joined warm planes and a compact bend light. Angular elbows, cap-like foliage, regular oil ridges, pale horizon fragments and ridged soil covers remain.

Narrow rust middles partially reunited split bands; small center turn became clearer.

title: River watch

title: Red mug, morning hush
